Title: MSOSH calls for safety audit after toddler's death at Victoria Bridge
Article:
IPOH: The Malaysian Society for Occupational Safety and Health (MSOSH) has called for a comprehensive technical investigation and safety audit by the relevant authorities following the death of a three-year-old boy who was believed to have fallen from the Victoria Bridge in Enggor, Kuala Kangsar, on Monday.
MSOSH president Datuk Ahmad Fakhrul Anuar Ismail said the audit should cover the entire visitor route, openings in the structure, the height and design of barriers, the condition of floors and walkways, lighting, warning signs, access controls and the suitability of the site for children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
He said risk assessment records, engineering inspection reports, maintenance schedules, damage reports, previous complaints and the approval status for public access should also be examined.
"The question that must be answered is not merely how the victim was able to fall, but whether the hazard had been identified earlier, who was responsible for controlling it and whether reasonable preventive measures had been taken," he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Fakhrul Anuar said the temporary closure of the site and the installation of barrier tape were appropriate immediate measures, but should not be regarded as a solution in themselves.
He said the site should only be reopened after an inspection by engineers or other competent parties had confirmed that all hazards had been addressed, including through the installation of child-friendly barriers, the sealing of all openings, improvements to walkways and the implementation of a regular inspection and maintenance system.
He said the tourism industry must also draw lessons from the incident, adding that the development of tourist destinations should not focus solely on historical value, visual appeal, promotion and visitor numbers.
"Local authorities, destination managers, tourism agencies, tour operators, event organisers and those promoting a location must exercise due diligence to ensure that the site is genuinely safe before inviting members of the public to visit," he said.
He said MSOSH had also proposed that safety audits be conducted at heritage sites and ageing structures nationwide that had been repurposed or opened as tourist attractions.
Priority, he said, should be given to locations involving risks of falls from height, ageing structures, narrow walkways, areas near water and sites that were not originally designed to accommodate large numbers of visitors.
Fakhrul Anuar also urged the victim's family to seek legal advice and consider appropriate legal action to obtain explanations, accountability and justice for the deceased.
He said such a move was not intended to pre-empt the outcome of investigations or draw conclusions against any party, but to ensure that the family's rights were protected and that the responsibilities of all relevant parties could be assessed through a fair and transparent legal process.
"Heritage must not only be preserved for its form and history, but must also be made safe for visitors. The tourism value of a location can never outweigh the value of a life.
"When members of the public are invited in, the responsibility for their safety begins before they set foot inside," he said.
He said MSOSH hoped the investigation would be carried out transparently and that its findings would translate into concrete corrective action.
"The goal is not merely to determine who was responsible after a tragedy has occurred, but to ensure that a similar incident does not happen again at any tourist destination in the country," he added.
On Monday, three-year-old Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was reported to have died after he was believed to have fallen about 5m from the more than 125-year-old bridge at around 6.30pm while
visiting the site with his father
.
The boy was believed to have been walking while holding his father's hand before falling through an opening in the bridge.
Following the incident, the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) immediately closed public access to the iron structure of the Victoria Bridge as a safety measure.

Title: Sersol sees new substantial shareholder as three directors quit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sersol Bhd has seen a shake-up in its shareholding and boardroom, with a new substantial shareholder emerging a day before three directors resigned from the company.
Peh Lon Pah @ Pei Tze Chiang acquired 100 million Sersol shares, equivalent to a 12.43 per cent stake, through an off-market transaction on Sept 1, according to a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
The acquisition makes Peh one of the company's major shareholders. The filing did not disclose the seller or the price paid for the shares.
The following day, executive director Datuk Mohamed Suffian Awang and non-independent non-executive directors Alan Ling Sie Kiong and Tan Tong Lang resigned.
All three cited other personal commitments as the reason for their departures and said there were no disagreements with the board or matters that needed to be brought to shareholders' attention.
MyBursa data showed Ice Age Property Sdn Bhd as Sersol's largest shareholder with 100 million shares, equivalent to a 12.43 per cent stake.
That is the same number of shares Peh disclosed acquiring through the off-market transaction on Sept 1.
However, Sersol's Bursa filing on Peh's acquisition did not identify the seller, and there is no disclosure establishing that the shares were acquired from Ice Age Property.
Mohamed Suffian's resignation filing, meanwhile, disclosed that he held an indirect interest in 100 million Sersol shares.
The filing did not specify the entity through which the indirect interest was held.
Tan's resignation also resulted in his departure from Sersol's audit, remuneration and nomination committees.
Following his exit, the audit committee comprises chairman Leong Lup Yan and member Tan Su Ning. Sersol said it was identifying a suitable candidate to fill the vacancy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel to drop by 5 sen from tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol, and unsubsidised RON95 petrol as well as unsubsidised diesel, will each decrease by 5 sen per litre for the period from Sept 3 to 9, 2026.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) in a statement today announced that RON97 is set at RM4.25 per litre compared to RM4.30 per litre previously, while RON95 has decreased to RM3.77 from RM3.82, and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.67 from RM4.72.
The MOF said that the decline reflects the world crude oil prices trading at lower levels for most of the calculation period under the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM), although prices increased again towards the end of the period due to geopolitical tensions in Middle East.
Although Brent crude oil prices have moderated from the peak levels of the Middle East conflict, the global refined petroleum product market remains tight due to disruptions in petroleum flow through the Strait of Hormuz, a reduction in refining capacity and fuel export restrictions, said MOF.
MOF said that these factors are expected to continue causing price fluctuations in the near term.
Meanwhile, China began to ease the export restrictions on refined petroleum products that were introduced since March 2026, but the supply of several petroleum products to the regional market has not yet fully returned to pre-conflict levels, even though exports started to increase from July.
The Madani government, according to the MOF, will continue to protect the people and businesses from the effects of global uncertainty by maintaining the targeted Budi Madani subsidies for eligible users.
Through Budi95, eligible recipients continue to pay RM1.99 per litre for RON95, with the government covering a subsidy of RM1.78 per litre or 47 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM3.77.
For Budi Diesel, recipients pay RM2.10 per litre with a government subsidy of RM2.57 per litre or 55 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.67.
Meanwhile, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre, respectively.
The MOF also announced that the monthly basic eligibility limit for Budi95 and Budi Diesel has been restored to 300 litres starting from Sept 1, while owners of diesel vehicles such as pickups and jeeps are eligible to receive an additional 100 litres, bringing the total eligibility to 400 litres per month.

Title: Bank manager fined RM40mil, jailed 7 years for fraud, money laundering
Article:
KUCHING: A relationship manager with an international bank was today sentenced to seven years' jail, fined RM40 million and ordered to receive 24 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges.
Judge Iris Awen Jon sentenced Kho Yung Kang, 39, after he pleaded guilty to 16 counts of fraud under Section 420 of the Penal Code and eight counts under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).
Kho pleaded guilty to defrauding eight senior citizens aged between 60 and 75 of RM1.58 million through a non-existent bond investment scheme, as well as committing money laundering at the bank where he worked between September 2022 and February 2024.
For each fraud charge, Kho was sentenced to between three and four years' jail and one stroke of the cane, with the jail terms to run concurrently from the date of his remand on May 23, 2025.
For each of the eight money laundering charges, he was sentenced to three years' jail, with the terms to run concurrently from today, fined RM5 million or four months' jail in default, and ordered to receive one stroke of the cane.
This brings the total sentence to seven years' jail, a RM40 million fine and 24 strokes of the cane. Kho failed to pay the fine.
According to the facts of the case, Kho was responsible for assisting customers with investments, including unit trusts, bonds and fixed deposits, as well as local and foreign remittances.
His modus operandi was to offer customers of the bank where he worked an investment scheme promising higher returns.
Based on the representation, Kho obtained the customers' signatures and biometric verification, but the funds were not used for investment purposes.
Instead, the money was transferred from the customers' accounts to third-party accounts via DuitNow, interbank transfers or Cashier's Orders without their knowledge or consent, for Kho's personal use.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Chuah Kai Sheng and Maryam Jamielah Ab Manaff appeared for the prosecution, while Kho was unrepresented.

Title: Ringgit weakens against US dollar, mixed against other major currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit continued to trade lower against the US dollar on Wednesday but strengthened against the British pound and the euro amid rising global bond yields and concerns over elevated government debt levels.
At 6pm, the ringgit was quoted at 4.0435/0475 against the US dollar compared with Tuesday's close of 4.0370/0410.
The market was closed on Monday for the Merdeka Day celebration.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said rising bond yields currently remained the main focus, particularly in developed markets.
"The context of higher long-term bond yields would include a higher inflation risk premium following the rise in crude oil prices, while global central banks could be seen as being behind the curve in tightening monetary conditions," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam elaborated that, above all, the concern was the lack of fiscal discipline to contain fiscal deficits and elevated government debt levels.
"Based on International Monetary Fund (IMF) data, gross government debt as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026 for the United States, the United Kingdom and Japan is expected to hit 125.8 per cent, 103.6 per cent and 204.4 per cent of GDP, respectively.
"It seems the market was a bit directionless as the mode does indicate a risk-off mode, but traders and investors were perplexed in seeking refuge in choosing the right asset class.
"On that note, the ringgit was hovering within a narrow band, ranging between RM4.0405 and RM4.0448 against the US dollar," he said.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit appreciated against the euro to 4.6787/6834 from yesterday's 4.6801/6847 and rose against the British pound to 5.4527/4581 from 5.4657/4711.
However, the local note weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5294/5321 from 2.5223/5250.
The local note traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It inched up against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.47 from 6.47/6.48 but declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1739/1773 from 3.1703/1736 on Tuesday and fell against the Thai baht to 12.1321/1488 from 12.1315/1483.
The ringgit also traded marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 227.6/227.9 from yesterday's close of 227.5/227.8.

Title: Putrajaya MRT Line service disrupted following signalling issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Train services on the Putrajaya MRT Line were disrupted this afternoon following a signalling system fault detected at 4.35pm.
Rapid KL, in a statement, said alternative train services and free shuttle buses had been activated to help commuters continue their journeys while waiting for a solution to the disruption.
"The alternative train services involve trains from Kentonmen station turning back at Raja Uda, while trains from Raja Uda will turn back at Chan Sow Lin.
"A shuttle train service is also operating between Chan Sow Lin and Putrajaya Sentral, with an expected frequency of five minutes.
"Free shuttle buses are operating between Kwasa Damansara and Kepong Baru, stopping at Kampung Selamat, Sungai Buloh, Damansara Damai, Sri Damansara Barat, Sri Damansara Sentral, Sri Damansara Timur and Metro Prima," it said in a social media post.
The bus service is expected to run every 15 to 20 minutes, depending on prevailing traffic conditions.
Rapid KL said its technical team was carrying out repair works to restore the power supply and return services to normal as soon as possible.
"To ensure passenger safety and smooth movement, auxiliary police personnel and station staff have been deployed at affected stations to provide assistance and guidance.
"Passengers requiring assistance may approach station staff or auxiliary police personnel on duty," it said.
Further updates will be issued through Rapid KL's official social media channels and the MyRapid PULSE application.

Title: Ramssol inks RM31mil AI, IT deal with Linear Channel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ramssol Group Bhd has teamed up with Linear Channel Sdn Bhd to provide information technology devices, artificial intelligence (AI) solutions and device monitoring software.
The RM30.94 million partnership, undertaken through Ramssol's unit Rams Aitech Sdn Bhd, will support Linear Channel's GreenElite Pro device-as-a-service programme.
Under the programme, Linear Channel contracts directly with small and medium enterprise customers to rent information technology equipment bundled with AI software and device fleet monitoring services.
Linear Channel will be responsible for customer relationships, deployment, servicing, billing and collection, while Rams Aitech will supply and license the relevant AI and device monitoring software, as well as provide the devices.
The partnership is covered by several agreements comprising a RM7.7 million foundation collaboration agreement entered into in March, a RM4.62 million equipment lease agreement, a RM12.36 million master reseller agreement and a RM6.27 million software licence agreement.
Under the arrangement, Linear Channel has committed to a 10,000-seat subscription base over 36 months, with about 2,000 new devices expected to be supplied by Rams Aitech.
The remaining 8,000 seats will be deployed on devices already owned by Linear Channel.
Linear Channel will pay Rams Aitech a minimum monthly charge of RM343,200 for the 10,000 seats.
Additional activated seats will be charged at RM34.32 per seat per month.
The agreements will run from Sept 2, 2026, to Sept 1, 2029.

Title: Haze leaves Kuching riverside traders counting losses
Article:
KUCHING: Haze has driven away more than clear skies in Kuching, with small traders at Esplanade Tebingan Kuching reporting a sharp drop in customers as residents increasingly stay indoors.
By 6pm today, rows of tables at the riverside stalls remained largely empty, a stark contrast to the usual evening crowd gathering for food, drinks and a stroll along the Sarawak River.
Trader Nony Rusley, who has operated her stall there since 2022, said her daily takings could previously reach RM1,000 but had fallen as the haze worsened.
"Usually, people would start arriving in large numbers from 3pm. There would still be customers until night.
"But now, even at 6pm, the area is still quiet. The difference has been very noticeable since the haze hit," she said when met.
She said the area, which normally attracted families in the late afternoon, had become noticeably quieter, with fewer people willing to spend time outdoors.
Another trader, who wished to be known only as Lan, said concerns over the health effects of the haze had prompted many families to limit outdoor activities.
He said the decline in visitors was particularly hard on small traders who relied heavily on the evening crowd.
"Usually, many people would come with their families. The children would play, and they would then stop by for food or drinks.
"Now, there are far fewer people. Perhaps they are afraid to go out because of the haze, especially since we have been hearing about the many cases of respiratory tract infections," he said.
The concerns come as upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) cases in Sarawak rise amid deteriorating air quality.
Yesterday, Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said monitoring at 15 sentinel health facilities statewide found average weekly URTI cases had risen from 1,717 at the beginning of the year to 1,752 recently.
She said the increase was more pronounced in mid-August, with the Southern Zone recording about 1,250 cases at its peak, followed by more than 1,000 in the Central Zone and nearly 400 in the Northern Zone.
From January to the end of August, the 15 sentinel facilities recorded 694,800 patient visits, including 64,688 URTI and 6,156 asthma cases.
For Lan, however, stopping business altogether is not an option despite the drop in customers.
He said the stall remained an important source of income and they could only continue operating while waiting for the haze to subside.
"We will continue doing business. If we stop and just stay at home, we will have no income.
"Our earnings have certainly been affected, but there is not much we can do. We will carry on while waiting for the situation to return to normal," he said.

Title: Teen feared drowned after telling friend he couldn't swim
Article:
MELAKA: An 18-year-old teen is feared drowned after disappearing while swimming at a beach near Prima Klebang here today.
His friend, Hakeem Putra Mahadi, 18, said the incident occurred at 3pm when the two, who had been friends since Form One, were spending time at the beach.
He said the teen, who was pursuing his studies at a college, had previously told him that he could not swim.
"We came to swim together and there was no one else in the area except a fisherman.
"He had told me that he could not swim, but his father had previously said that he could swim," he said when contacted today.
Hakeem said the situation turned tense when his friend suddenly appeared to be struggling in the water before disappearing.
"I tried to save him but was unsuccessful before immediately calling the emergency services for help," he said.
Meanwhile, the Melaka Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call about the incident at 3.03pm.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Assistant Fire Superintendent II Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said a team led by Operations Commander Senior Fire Officer I Mohd Soffian Hassan rushed to the scene.
He said the search and rescue operation involved 14 personnel from the Melaka Tengah Fire and Rescue Station, including the Water Rescue Team, with assistance from the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and police.
"The victim has yet to be found," he said.

Title: PPC orders probe into Teluk Bahang ferry collision
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: The Penang Port Commission (PPC) has ordered a special investigation into the cause of the Teluk Bahang ferry collision that injured 21 people last night.
PPC chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the team, comprising the commission and ferry operator Penang Port Sdn Bhd, would conduct an objective, transparent and professional investigation.
"The findings will be reported comprehensively to the public. We will not shy away from any issues and will take follow-up action based on the investigation findings," he said today.
The incident
occurred at 8.40pm yesterday
when the Teluk Bahang ferry, travelling from Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda in George Town to Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim in Butterworth, collided with cargo vessel MV Mekar Jaya within Penang Port limits.
The impact caused several motorcycles on the ferry to overturn, while some passengers were injured.
Yeoh said he rushed to Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim shortly after the incident to assess the situation and obtain an initial report before visiting the victims at hospital.
"Based on preliminary information, 21 people were injured and all the victims were taken to hospital for further treatment," he said.
He added that the relevant parties had been instructed to gather information immediately and assist with compensation arrangements for the victims.
Yeoh said the ferry operator had also been directed to review its operating procedures and safety mechanisms.
"Follow-up measures, including improvements to prevent a recurrence, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation," he added.
PPC will also work with Penang Port Sdn Bhd and relevant agencies to ensure follow-up measures are carried out and ferry services continue as usual following the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macau chief executive begins working visit to Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Macau Special Administrative Region Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai will undertake a four-day working visit to Malaysia from today to Sept 5.
The Foreign Ministry, in a statement today, said that during the visit, Sam is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"Both sides are expected to exchange views on Malaysia-Macau bilateral relations under the framework of One Country, Two Systems, as well as review current developments in bilateral cooperation and discuss the direction of cooperation, particularly in trade and economic affairs, tourism and culture, and people-to-people ties," the statement said.
This will be Sam's first visit to Malaysia since assuming office as Macau's fourth chief executive in 2024.
He will be accompanied by his partner, Wong He Peng, Secretary for Economy and Finance Ng Wai Han, senior government officials, as well as representatives from various sectors, including the economy, trade, education, tourism and culture.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Macau was valued at RM367.7 million (US$85.8 million), an increase of 73.6 per cent compared with 2024.

Title: PHB expands AHB fund with 400mil new units
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) has announced the issuance of 400 million new units of Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) for subscription by Bumiputera investors, raising the fund's total units to 5.4 billion.
PHB said the additional units reaffirmed its commitment to expanding opportunities for Bumiputera to gain beneficial ownership of quality commercial properties through investments in strategically located commercial real estate assets nationwide.
The latest issuance marks AHB's sixth expansion since its establishment in 2010, when the fund had an initial size of one billion units.
"The latest issuance is supported by value injections from two PHB assets, the recently acquired Aurelius Hospital in Alor Setar, Kedah, and the revaluation of the Maersk logistics building in Shah Alam," it said in a statement.
AHB, Malaysia's first Shariah-compliant property-based unit trust fund, is backed by a portfolio of prime commercial properties that generate rental income and provide sustainable returns to unitholders.
The minimum investment in AHB is RM100, while the maximum investment limit is RM1 million per individual. The fund is managed by PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM).
Investors can subscribe to AHB units at authorised distributor branches nationwide, including Maybank, AmBank, AmBank Islamic, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd.
Existing Maybank customers can also subscribe through the Maybank2u website, where they can check their current unit holdings and subscribe to the new units.

Title: Pandemic delays behind payment backlog, says Rural Development Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) has denied claims by the Finance Ministry (MoF) that it overspent its parliamentary allocation, saying payment backlogs stemmed from delayed commitments made during the Covid-19 pandemic, rather than financial mismanagement.
KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil said portraying the ministry as having spent beyond its allocation gave an inaccurate picture of government financial procedures.
"Government financial procedure does not allow any ministry to simply spend beyond its approved allocation. Every expenditure is governed by the Integrated Government Financial Management and Accounting System (iGFMAS), while development projects require explicit approval from the Economy Ministry.
"Claims of irregular spending are subject to Treasury Instructions, which prevent unapproved project disbursements," he said in a statement.
Earlier, MoF
refuted claims
that KKDW's allocation for rural road projects had been cut or restricted, saying all approved funds had been fully channelled.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said recent payment delays to contractors stemmed from KKDW having almost exhausted its current-year allocation after years of spending beyond its approved parliamentary allocations.
"Every ministry is responsible for planning and managing its expenditure based on the annual budget approved by Parliament.
"There have been no restrictions placed on KKDW's allocation for rural roads; the funds have been fully disbursed. The payment constraints faced by contractors occurred because the current year's allocation has already been almost entirely spent," he said.
Fadzmel said MoF's figures did not include data from 2019 to 2021, when "Acceptance Letters" were issued for rural projects despite pandemic-related disruptions.
"As construction resumed in subsequent years, contractor payment claims carried over into 2023 through 2026.
"When contractors complete work, the government has a contractual obligation to pay according to progress. Ongoing projects cannot simply be halted because the annual budget allocation is nearly exhausted," he said.
He also clarified that the RM300 million released by MoF was not additional funding, but delayed operational allocations disbursed through an Authority to Spend letter on Sept 1 following intervention by the Deputy Prime Minister.
While welcoming the release, Fadzmel said the RM300 million remained insufficient to settle all outstanding contractor claims, with final budget adjustments only expected at the end of 2026.
He added that rural project funds were not paid directly by KKDW to contractors, but channelled through implementing agencies such as the Public Works Department (PWD).
"This should not become a dispute between ministries. The priority is finding an immediate resolution to existing payment commitments, and KKDW will continue working with MoF to clear all outstanding obligations," he said.

Title: Sultan Nazrin graces Maha 2026
Article:
SERDANG: The Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism (Maha) Exhibition 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS).
Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim and Raja Kecil Besar Raja Azlan Muzzaffar Shah accompanied him on the visit.
Sultan Nazrin's arrival at 10.45am was received by Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Perak Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid, as well as Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
Sultan Nazrin, Tuanku Zara and Raja Azlan visited several booths at the Perak Pavilion.
Thy also mingled with several exhibitors and entrepreneurs at the site, in addition to visiting the
Laman Padi
(padi pavilion) and
Laman Herba
(herb pavilion).
The 101st edition of Maha is being held for 10 days, from Aug 28 to Sept 6.
The biennial event is the country's main agricultural sector platform, bringing together industry players, government agencies, entrepreneurs, as well as research and higher education institutions to highlight innovation, technology and business opportunities in the agrifood sector.

Title: Cargo vessel hits Sungai Johor Bridge in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A cargo vessel is believed to have struck the Sungai Johor Bridge along the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE) here today.
The Malaysian-flagged oil-products tanker hit the bridge at 2.35pm at KM48.9 westbound, along the Penawar-Pasir Gudang stretch.
No injuries were reported.
The New Straits Times learnt that the bridge structure remained intact, with no major defects or damage reported.
The vessel has since been moved, NST was told.
The SDE operator is expected to issue an official statement soon.

Title: Deadly rough seas: Three beach incidents in Kota Tinggi in four days
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Three people have drowned and three teenagers remain missing following three separate incidents at beaches in the district in just four days.
The authorities, including the Fire and Rescue Department and police, have urged the public to stay out of the sea amid rough conditions.
Four 16-year-old boys were swept away while swimming at Pantai Tanjung Lompat, Bandar Desaru here, this morning.
The body of Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, 16, was recovered by search and rescue members at 1.25pm, about 800m from where the teenagers were reported missing.
The three others
still missing
are Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian and Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal.
The incident came four days after a
man and his 8-year-old son
drowned while swimming at a beach campsite in Kampung Punggai, Pengerang, on Sunday.
The victims were Mohammad Nizam Zain, 33, and his son, Muhammad Zamri Mikhail. The father is believed to have drowned while trying to save his son.
On the same day, at 10.04am, four people got into difficulties while swimming at a beach campsite in Bandar Penawar.
They were Samsudeen Hasan, 44, his son Muhamad Syakir, 16, and sisters Nur Qaira Izzara Abdul Latif, 16, and Nur Qasseh Insyeerah Abdul Latif, 14.
All four were rescued by members of the public at the scene.
The three incidents occurred during the school holidays, with the victims taking the opportunity to camp and swim at the district's beaches.
A check at Pantai Tanjung Lompat today found rough seas and strong winds, with the district currently experiencing the transition towards the northeast monsoon.
Deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad urged the public to put safety first and avoid entering the sea when conditions were unsafe.
"We advise the public to temporarily stop swimming in the sea as conditions are currently dangerous.
"Today, the winds are quite strong and the waves are rough, posing a risk to beachgoers," he said.
He said strong winds, rough waves and rocky sections of the beach were also hampering the search and rescue operation for the missing teens.
About 30 personnel from seven agencies are involved in the operation, including the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency, marine police, Civil Defence Force and the Health Ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas to sustain production at 2mil barrels of oil equivalent per day through 2028
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) aims to sustain Malaysia's oil and gas production at two million barrels of oil equivalent per day (mmboe/d) through 2028, said its president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz today.
He said the target would be anchored in continued investment across exploration, deep-water development, and enhanced recovery from Petronas' producing fields.
"Holding that line, however, has meant finding new ways to work with partners rather than just relying on old formulas. Our own experience with Searah Ltd, the regional venture with Eni, reflects that shift.
"It is built not simply around sharing leadership, but also combining capital, technical expertise, and taking risks together to pursue opportunities at a scale neither partner would have done alone," he said in his keynote address at the opening ceremony of Oil and Gas Asia (OGA) 2026 today.
Across its portfolio, Tengku Muhammad Taufik said the national oil company is applying the same approach through partnerships, technical collaborations and alternative commercial structures tailored to the circumstances of individual opportunities. He noted that the best outcomes have come from combining Petronas' existing knowledge and capabilities with those of equally capable partners amid an increasingly daunting operating environment.
Tengku Muhammad Taufik said the same principle should extend beyond operators to the entire oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) ecosystem, which has built considerable capabilities over four decades of operating in Malaysia. "The strength that you have built needs a much wider stage. A much wider stage than the one that you have traditionally competed in," he added.
However, he cautioned that succeeding on a bigger stage would require more than technical competence, with OGSE players needing significantly higher productivity, stronger financial resilience, greater digital maturity and sound governance to be regarded as trusted partners. "More importantly, you must also have the conviction to invest ahead of this demand. Are we collectively connected enough, capable enough, competitive enough?" he asked.
Tengku Muhammad Taufik said competitiveness should not be measured merely by a company's ability to win its next tender under favourable market conditions, but by whether it can remain relevant over the next decade as technology, workforce requirements, and the industry's capital landscape evolve.  "Can we collectively sustain our momentum at the pace, scale and technical depth that the next decade will now not only ask, but demand of you?" he added.
He said meeting that standard was as much a question of timing as it was of intent, including investing in people and improving productivity even when contracts were not plentiful. Industry players, he added, should also adopt digital tools and new ways of working that leading operators elsewhere already regard as standard, while building the financial resilience needed to withstand future downturns.
Tengku Muhammad Taufik also called on Malaysian OGSE companies to venture beyond their traditional markets and view developments elsewhere as opportunities rather than merely challenges or competitive pressure. He highlighted that there is much to learn from leading energy and services companies across Asia and beyond, just as international players could learn from the capabilities Malaysian companies had developed domestically.
Opportunities in carbon capture, low-emission shipping, frontier exploration, deep-water development and digital energy systems, he reckons, are open to companies that are ready to seize them. "I have the confidence that Malaysian companies can be among those ready and can be among those who help build the partnerships required to deliver them," he said.
Tengku Muhammad Taufik said Petronas, for its part, remained committed to working with industry players to build the necessary runway, open new frontiers and provide the ecosystem with greater visibility to plan ahead. "But all of this can only serve and benefit those of you who dare to take flight," he added.
He called on industry players to match that commitment by investing with conviction, taking calculated risks and positioning themselves as partners in shaping the industry's future direction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar warns US-Iran strikes risk wider Middle East conflict
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged the United States and Iran to immediately halt further escalation and return to diplomacy amid renewed hostilities between the two countries.
He warned that the latest exchange of strikes, which has extended beyond the immediate parties and into other states in the region, risks drawing the wider Middle East into an even more destructive conflict.
He said the party with the greatest capacity to shape events bears a particular responsibility to exercise restraint and prevent further escalation.
"The sovereignty of other states cannot be cast aside. No military objective justifies exposing civilians to an expanding conflict," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar also cautioned against economic measures that inflict hardship on civilians and impede diplomatic engagement, saying such actions risk exacerbating rather than resolving the crisis.
"I urge the United States and Iran to halt further escalation and return immediately to diplomacy and the understandings reached in June," he said.
He said the conflict could ultimately be resolved only through political and diplomatic means, adding that the world must not be made to pay the price for a wider regional war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls a test of BN-PN cooperation, says analyst
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka state election will serve as a test of whether cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) is built on a larger political goal or merely holds up as long as it does not touch on each party's individual seat interests.
Sekretariat Tanahair secretary-general Dr Armin Baniaz Pahamin said following developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan, the public wanted to see whether both coalitions could translate their spirit of cooperation into an arrangement that was structured, fair and durable.
He said BN had reason to be confident in Melaka given the state's strong Umno grassroots organisation, with the coalition's landslide win in the last state election cementing its position as the dominant force there.
However, he said past strength should not be used as a reason to shut the door on negotiations, as voting patterns had shifted, public sentiment continued to move and three-cornered contests could produce unexpected results.
"PN should not enter negotiations demanding an equal seat split without taking into account the reality of local strength on the ground.
"Fairness in negotiations does not mean each side must receive the same number of seats. Fairness instead means each party is given reasonable space based on its ground machinery, track record of support, candidate suitability and probability of winning," he said in a statement.
He said among the formulas that could be considered was a split of 20 seats for BN and eight for PN, or 21 seats for BN and seven for PN, based on winnability.
However, he said the figures should not be treated as a fixed, predetermined outcome, as the final seat distribution must be decided based on the latest electoral data, ground machinery strength, candidate acceptance and the likelihood of winning in each constituency.
On PN, he said the coalition first needed to finalise who would be mandated to represent it in negotiations, as well as which component parties would contest in the election.
"This step is important so that seat allocation is not overshadowed by internal uncertainty within the coalition.
"In return, if PN is prepared to compromise in Melaka, that willingness should be reciprocated by BN in states where Pas and PN hold a stronger position.
"The same principle should also apply to seat distribution, which must reflect the actual strength of each party according to local realities, rather than a uniform formula applied across all states," he said.
He said Umno and BN had two clear choices, whether to contest alone to prove they could still control Melaka without PN's help, or to accept that a win in one state was merely part of a larger journey towards the 16th general election (GE16).
He said the first option might bring satisfaction to the party, but the second carried the potential to build an alliance capable of changing the government at the federal level.
"PN also needs to choose between measuring its own strength and building a joint victory, because contesting more seats might project boldness, but political courage is not measured by the number of candidates fielded.
"It is measured by the ability to convert support into victory, form a government and implement policy.
"There is no benefit in contesting in many areas if vote-splitting ultimately hands victory to the opposing side," he said.
He said if BN-PN negotiations failed, three-cornered contests would almost certainly take place in many areas.
Under such circumstances, he said, the Malay vote would split, machinery resources would be spent attacking each other, and attention would shift away from public issues, administrative performance and the state's direction towards infighting between parties that should otherwise have much in common.

Title: Wildfire haze forces 1.4 million Indonesian students into remote learning
Article:
JAKARTA: Around 1.4 million students in six Indonesian provinces have shifted to online learning due to poor air quality triggered by forest and land fires, an official said on Wednesday.
As of Sept 2, around 1.43 million students from 12,874 schools in six of the provinces hit hardest by forest and land fires have been studying remotely, Gogot Suharwoto, an education ministry official, told the media.
Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze caused by wildfire in the six provinces, which include Riau, Jambi and South Sumatra on the island of Sumatra, as well as West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan, and South Kalimantan on Borneo.
Of the 1.43 million students, 1.1 million are in West Kalimantan, Gogot said, the province that has recorded the most extensive wildfires so far this year.
The remote learning period will last from Aug 31 until Sept 4 and will be continuously evaluated every three days, Gogot said.
The decision to conduct online learning would be based on the Air Pollution Standard Index in each region, he said.
Remote learning would be imposed when the index exceeds 200 in a particular location, Gogot added.
A majority of regions in Kalimantan recorded air pollution readings in excess of 200 on Wednesday, with some even exceeding 1,000, Forestry Ministry data showed. Southeast Pontianak region in West Kalimantan province was the worst hit, with a reading of 1,023.
Indonesia's air quality classification system considers readings above 300 as "hazardous."
"School principals are authorised to take immediate action in urgent situations. They do not have to wait until conditions worsen or spend too long consulting with other authorities," Gogot said.
Forestry Ministry data showed that about 200,000 hectares of land were burned by wildfires in the first seven months of the year, nearly doubling in July alone.
Wildfires burned around 73,310 hectares of land in six priority provinces, according to Forestry Ministry data.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UKM denies convicted ex-student is university staff
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) has denied that Nur Fitri Azmeer Nordin, who was previously convicted in Britain of possessing child sexual abuse material, is a staff member at the university.
In a statement today, UKM said Nur Fitri had completed his Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) at the university in 2021.
"UKM denies that Nur Fitri Azmeer is a UKM staff member.
"As a higher education institution, UKM is committed to ensuring a conducive and professional learning environment for all students," it said.
The clarification followed a viral social media post in which an X user urged UKM students to inform their parents about the alleged presence of Nur Fitri, claiming he was an academic at the university.
Nur Fitri, who previously studied at Imperial College London, made headlines in 2015 after he was sentenced to nine months in prison in Britain for possessing more than 30,000 images and videos of child sexual abuse.
The Southwark Crown Court sentenced him after he pleaded guilty to 17 charges of possessing child sexual abuse material with intent to distribute.
At the time of his arrest, police found that the mathematics scholar, who was studying in Britain on a scholarship, possessed 601 Category A images and videos involving the sexual abuse of children, as well as hundreds of Category B and C materials.

Title: Mudajaya, China Communications Construction dispute widens with RM17.6mil claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mudajaya Group Bhd's unit, Mudajaya Corp Bhd, has served a second payment claim against China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd (CCC) totalling RM17.56 million amid an ongoing dispute linked to the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the claim relates to unpaid certified amounts under CCC's interim payment certificates, under-certified and uncertified work done, uncertified variations and wrongful contra charges.
"The company further wishes to update that the arbitration proceeding is still at its early stage, and parties are in the process of appointing an arbitrator," it said.
Mudajaya filed an adjudication in December 2025 under the Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 (CIPAA), seeking RM10.95 million from CCC over under-certified claims for Package 3 of the ECRL.
On May 31, the adjudicator ruled in favour of Mudajaya, awarding it RM7.77 million, together with interest, costs and expenses.
However, CCC did not make the payment, prompting Mudajaya to apply to the High Court to enforce the adjudication decision.
CCC subsequently commenced arbitration proceedings against Mudajaya, seeking a declaration that it was not obliged to pay the RM7.77 million.
It also claimed RM22.75 million from Mudajaya for additional costs, losses, liquidated damages, management fees and interest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Treat haze as annual health threat, not seasonal nuisance, pharmacists urge public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians should treat transboundary haze as a recurring public health threat and prepare for it before air quality deteriorates, the Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) said.
Its president, Professor Amrahi Buang, said families should not regard haze merely as a temporary inconvenience, particularly when exposure to fine particulate matter continues over several days.
He said children, older adults, pregnant women and people with chronic respiratory or cardiovascular conditions should reduce time spent outdoors and avoid strenuous activity when the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings worsen.
"Those with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or heart conditions should not wait until their breathing problems become severe before seeking professional advice," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Amrahi said people with chronic illnesses should ensure they have enough prescribed medication, including inhalers, and review whether they are using inhalers correctly.
He said ordinary surgical masks did not provide adequate protection against PM2.5 — microscopic airborne particles measuring 2.5 micrometres or less that are commonly associated with haze.
"Where outdoor exposure cannot be avoided, the public should use a properly fitted N95 respirator or an equivalent mask, with no gaps around the edges that allow unfiltered air to enter."
Amrahi said community pharmacies in affected areas were ready to handle increased demand for advice and treatment for mild irritation, including sore throats and eye discomfort.
He said pharmacists could also check medication adherence, advise patients on inhaler use and refer those experiencing severe respiratory distress to clinics or hospitals without delay.
For indoor protection, Amrahi said air purifiers fitted with True HEPA filters could reduce PM2.5 levels if they were appropriately sized for the room, maintained regularly and used with windows and doors closed.
He urged households to build an annual haze-readiness routine by keeping certified N95 masks and essential medication on hand, servicing air-conditioning units and purifiers before the dry season, and checking the Department of Environment's official API updates daily before planning outdoor activities.
Haze has affected much of the country, with several areas in Sarawak recording
hazardous API readings
and unhealthy air quality reported in Sabah, Labuan and parts of Peninsular Malaysia.
The haze has been linked mainly to
forest and land fires
in Kalimantan and Sumatra, with prevailing winds carrying smoke into Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Felda pledges cooperation in MACC probe into seven cases
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Felda has pledged cooperation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in the graft buster's probe involving the agency and its subsidiaries.
In a statement, Felda said it respected the ongoing investigations and would continue to assist MACC to ensure the probes were conducted transparently, fairly and comprehensively.
"We will not compromise on any acts of corruption, misappropriation, abuse of power or breaches of the law that could jeopardise the interests of settlers and the institution," it said in a statement today.
The agency also urged all parties to respect the investigation process.
The statement comes after MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri
Abd Halim Aman
said seven Felda-related cases previously investigated or highlighted in forensic reports had been reopened following the emergence of new information.
Halim said six of the cases involved new investigations, while the case involving Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd was a continuation of a previous probe.
The seven cases involve Dataran Aras Sdn Bhd, Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd, Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites, Park City Grand Plaza Kensington, Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd, Felda House and Grand Felda House, as well as the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
Among them, the Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites acquisition had previously led to the prosecution of former Felda chairman Tan Sri Mohd Isa Abdul Samad, who faced nine corruption charges involving RM3.09 million in relation to the RM160 million hotel purchase.
The KLVC project, meanwhile, involved concerns over the transfer of Felda land ownership and project governance, although a 2018 MACC investigation found no elements of corruption or abuse of power in the land transfer agreement.
Halim had also suggested that Felda appoint its own forensic audit team to examine governance issues and misconduct detected within the agency.
He said such a team could assist MACC in its investigation, while other enforcement agencies should also examine the weaknesses identified instead of leaving the investigations solely to MACC.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously called for weaknesses and problems in Felda's management to be addressed, with firm action taken to strengthen governance and prevent similar issues from recurring.
He said a special task force investigating issues involving the Felda has begun its work, with its findings expected to be announced once the investigations are completed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5.5-magnitude quake hits northeast of New Zealand's Milford Sound
Article:
WELLINGTON: A 5.5-magnitude earthquake struck 40 kilometres northeast of Milford Sound on New Zealand's South Island on Wednesday, the country's earthquake monitoring agency reported.
The quake, at a depth of 5km, struck at 6.13pm local time and was classified as moderate, according to GeoNet, which said nearly 7,000 people had reported feeling it.
